questionText: Do you favor increasing the annual tax on the assessed value of all taxable real property situated in Bethel Township from .027 mills to .037 mills to aid in maintaining the Rachel Kohl Community Library?
officialStatement: In 2006 voters in Bethel Township instituted an annual tax on the assessed value of all taxable real property situated in Bethel Township at the rate of .05 mills, which equates to $5 per $100,000 of assessed value, to support Rachel Kohl Community Library (the "Library Tax"). In 2021, when Delaware County reassessed the value of all taxable real estate, state law required the Township to reduce the Library Tax millage to .027 mills. At the current rate of .027 mills, the Library Tax costs $2.70 per $100,000 of assessed value annually. The purpose of the foregoing question is to determine whether the Township should increase the Library Tax to .037 mills. The proposed rate of .037 mills would cost $3.70 per $100,000 of assessed value, an increase of $1.00 per $100,000 per year. This would provide the Rachel Kohl Community Library (the "Library") with a total tax revenue from Bethel Township of just over $5.00 per resident in Bethel Township, which is the level required throughout Library's service area to qualify for Quality Libraries Aid, a form of additional funding from the Commonwealth.

questionText: Shall debt in the maximum principal amount of up to $120 million be authorized for purposes of financing land conservation, including protecting drinking water sources, water quality in rivers and creeks, wildlife habitat, conserving trees to protect air quality, conserving wetlands to prevent flooding, providing greenways and parks, protecting natural areas from development, and related costs, to be incurred by the County as debt approved by the voters,requiring public disclosure and annual independent audits?
officialStatement: This ballot question, if approved by the voters, would authorize the County to borrow up to $120 million for projects that protect water quality, natural areas, and wildlife habitat within the County. The projects could include purchasing land to preserve open space, creating new parks, improving existing parks and outdoor recreation areas, building trails for walking, hiking, and biking, and other projects related to environmental conservation and protecting natural areas from development. If approved by the voters, the County could choose to borrow all of the amount approved by the voters, or only some of the amount approved, and can choose to fund some or all of the listed types of projects. If the voters approve the question, the County commits to make full public disclosure of the projects funded with the money it borrows and to provide annual audits by an independent auditor of all spending.
